datasets.name: Global Inventory of Floras and Traits (GIFT)

checked.method: GET GIFT API query=lists, query=species, query=traits_meta; GET landing

variables_present: native/naturalized-flagged plant checklists per geographic entity
variables_missing: over-water distances between entities (not seen in endpoints queried)
pairwise similarity matrix (must be computed from species-by-list data)
datasets.scope: Worldwide regional and island floras; list-level API open without login
datasets.evidence: GIFT API https://gift.uni-goettingen.de/api/extended/index.php?query=lists returned 200 (JSON array; first 400 KB read) of list records with fields ref_ID, type (Flora/Checklist), native_indicated, natural_indicated, entity_ID, geo_entity, entity_class (first record: 'Ashmore Reef', entity_class 'Island'); query=species returned 200 with work_species names; query=traits_meta returned 200 (Woodiness_1 count 249,169). Landing page returned 200 (5,520 bytes). Pairwise distance fields were not seen in the endpoints I queried.

The abstract says the 249 islands were assembled from GIFT and GloNAF. File download via API returned 401, so columns were not read.

summary: Native regional and island floras with an island label are open through the GIFT API, and GloNAF (Zenodo) lists human-introduced aliases for 1,343 regions. No fetched resource holds over-water distances, pairwise floristic similarity and dispersal events together; island-level summaries (Bach 2022) and regional studies (Danish islands) cover parts at limited scope.
next_step: Pull species-by-list data from GIFT for island and continental entities, compute great-circle or over-water distances from entity coordinates, and use GloNAF to flag human-introduced species before pre-registering the distance-decay test.
obstacles_confirmed: No single table of pairwise native-species sharing versus ocean distance was found.
POWO is behind a bot challenge (403) for scripted access.
Human-introduced species are recorded separately in GloNAF; mechanisms (currents, birds, driftwood) are not variables in any flora table.
